_comment: Data/Content/lessons/w<week>d<day>.json - the AUTHORED half of a lesson. Hand-written, and outside the generated tree for the same reason solutions/ and variations/ are: the notebooks are the master for teaching content, so anything written here would be erased by the next `npm run import` if it lived under Data/Content/weeks/. An overlay is purely ADDITIVE - it supplies the three sections that give every lesson the same shape and has NO way to remove or rewrite a generated block, so a notebook stays the only place the course's teaching can change. Merged by applyOverlay() in scripts/lesson-overlay.ts, which runs both inside the importer and standalone via `npm run overlay`.

parts._comment: Keyed by part number as a string, '1' to '4'. A part with no entry is left exactly as imported. STRICT: a mistyped key is an error rather than a silent no-op, because these files are hand-written and a quietly ignored key reads as 'the overlay did nothing' with nothing to explain why.

at_a_glance._comment: Markdown. Opens the lesson, inserted directly after its H1: what this part is for, what the learner will have done by the end, and what it assumes. Optional.

checkpoints._comment: Retrieval practice, inserted before the recap and before any trailing 'What's next' section. Optional; 2-3 is the norm on a concept part, and a practice part usually has none because its problems already do the work.

question._comment: Markdown. One question, answerable from this lesson alone.

options._comment: 2-5 answers. A distractor has to be something a learner could plausibly believe after reading the lesson - not filler.

answer._comment: 0-based index into options. Validated against options.length by the contract, not just by eye.

explanation._comment: Shown after answering, right or wrong. Says WHY, and points at the part of the lesson it came from.

recap._comment: Markdown. Closes the lesson, after the checkpoints: the few things worth carrying forward, scannable. Optional.
